hero.headline: SEC Proposes Ending Climate Disclosure Rule for Public Companies
hero.body:
The Securities and Exchange Commission proposed eliminating a regulation that would have required publicly traded companies to disclose climate change risks. The rule targeted whether companies faced significant risks from climate change and its effects.

The proposal marks a reversal for the agency on corporate climate transparency. The original regulation aimed to standardize how public companies report climate-related financial risks to investors.

The disclosure requirement would have applied to all publicly traded companies in the United States. Under the rule, firms would have needed to report whether climate change posed material risks to their operations, supply chains, or long-term business prospects.

The SEC has not specified when a final decision on the proposal will be made. The agency typically allows a public comment period before finalizing regulatory changes.

Environmental advocates had supported the disclosure rule as a way to give investors better information about climate risks. Business groups raised concerns about the compliance costs and feasibility of accurately quantifying climate-related risks.

The proposal comes amid broader debates about corporate environmental reporting standards. Several states and foreign jurisdictions have implemented their own climate disclosure requirements for large companies operating within their borders.

Investors have increasingly pressed companies to provide more detailed information about how climate change might affect their business models. Major institutional investors have argued that climate risks represent material financial information that shareholders need to make informed decisions.

The outcome of the SEC proposal could influence how American companies approach climate risk reporting. Even without a federal mandate, some large corporations have voluntarily disclosed climate-related risks in their annual reports and sustainability statements.

cards.headline: Israel seizes historic Lebanese castle as ground offensive expands
cards.teaser: Israeli forces captured Beaufort Castle in southern Lebanon, a fortress that symbolized its previous occupation of the country.
cards.body:
Israeli forces have captured Beaufort Castle, a 12th-century fortress in southern Lebanon that overlooks the border with northern Israel. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu characterized the seizure as a "decisive shift" in the military campaign against Hezbollah.

The castle holds symbolic weight for both nations. It previously served as a landmark during Israel's occupation of southern Lebanon, which ended in 2000. The capture has revived difficult memories in both countries as the conflict with Hezbollah continues to escalate. The move suggests Israel may maintain an extended military presence in the region.

cards.headline: Colombia votes in presidential election that could reshape US relations
cards.teaser: Colombians began voting in a high-stakes presidential election testing the legacy of the country's first leftist leader.
cards.body:
Colombians are casting ballots in the first round of a presidential election that will determine the country's direction on peace and US relations. The vote comes after months of tension between outgoing leftist President Gustavo Petro and US President Donald Trump, with candidates offering starkly different visions for the nation's future.

The election serves as a referendum on Petro's policies a decade after Colombia signed a historic peace agreement with the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (Farc). Voters must choose between candidates with radically diverging approaches to addressing the country's decades-long conflict.

cards.teaser: A review shows the United States has been involved in multiple military operations globally

cards.headline: US military strike kills three in fourth eastern Pacific boat attack this week
cards.body:
The US military conducted another strike on a vessel in the eastern Pacific Ocean on Tuesday, killing three people. This marks the fourth such attack this week, according to officials with US Southern Command.

The military said the vessel was suspected of operating in drug trafficking routes. In a post on social media, Southern Command stated that intelligence had confirmed the boat was transiting along known narco-trafficking routes in the eastern Pacific and was engaged in narco-trafficking operations. The command described those killed as "male narco-terrorists," though it did not provide identifying details or evidence of their involvement in drug trafficking.

Southern Command alleged the vessel was operated by "Designated Terrorist Organizations" without identifying which groups. The military said no US forces were harmed in the operation.

This latest strike brings the total death toll from such military operations to more than 200 since September. A similar attack on Monday in the Caribbean Sea killed two additional people. The death toll now stands at 205 according to some reports, though exact figures vary across sources.

The Trump administration has escalated what it describes as measures against "narcoterrorism" in recent weeks. The administration has not released definitive evidence that the targeted vessels were actually involved in drug trafficking, which has prompted significant debate about the legality of the operations.

Rights groups and human rights organizations have raised serious questions about the strikes. Human Rights Watch and Amnesty International have labeled the operations as "unlawful extrajudicial killings." The American Civil Liberties Union has described the Trump administration's assertions about the targeted vessels as "unsubstantiated, fear-mongering claims."

Experts and human rights advocates both within the United States and internationally have challenged whether the strikes comply with international law. The lack of transparency regarding evidence of drug trafficking or terrorist connections has fueled ongoing criticism of the military campaign.

The eastern Pacific Ocean has long served as a transit route for smuggling operations moving narcotics northward toward North America. The frequency of strikes this week represents an intensification of US military operations targeting suspected drug trafficking vessels in the region.

The operations appear designed as part of a broader enforcement effort against maritime drug trafficking. However, the escalating death toll combined with questions about evidence and due process has drawn increased scrutiny from advocacy groups and legal experts who question whether the military strikes align with international humanitarian law and established rules of engagement.

Southern Command has not provided detailed information about the identities of those killed or the specific circumstances surrounding each strike.

cards.headline: Newark mayor orders curfew around immigration detention center after clashes
cards.teaser: Newark Mayor Ras Baraka imposed a mandatory curfew for a half mile around Delaney Hall after protests over the immigration detention center turned violent.
cards.body:
Newark Mayor Ras Baraka imposed a curfew around Delaney Hall following clashes between protesters and Trump supporters. The order covers a half mile radius around the immigration detention facility.

A hunger strike at the ICE facility entered its ninth day as demonstrators faced off outside. New Jersey Governor Sherrill blamed outsiders for the violence, while reports indicate protesters had established an organized logistics operation before the demonstrations began. Nearly 800 people were arrested in the incidents, with 219 injured including 57 police officers according to some reports.

cards.headline: Meteor explodes over Massachusetts, creating sonic boom heard across Northeast
cards.body:
A meteor exploded over the northeastern United States on Saturday afternoon, producing a powerful sonic boom that residents reported hearing across a wide geographic area. NASA confirmed the meteor caused the explosion and indicated that meteorite fragments may have fallen near Cape Cod Bay.

The fireball streaked across the sky at around 2:06 pm ET, visible to multiple observers who captured it on camera. The explosion was so significant that it shook houses in the region and appeared clearly in satellite imagery, lighting up the sky during daylight hours. The incident generated reports from locations stretching across multiple states and into Canada, including areas as far south as Delaware and as far north as Montreal.

Residents in the affected region initially puzzled over the loud booms, with many uncertain about the source of the disturbance. Some thought the shaking and noise might have come from other causes before NASA identified the meteor as responsible. Reports poured in from across the northeastern corridor, indicating the meteor's trajectory covered a substantial distance before fragmenting.

According to NASA's analysis, data placed the initial visibility of the fireball above Lake Erie. The meteor was a small asteroid measuring nearly 6 feet in diameter and weighing about 7 tons. It traveled at approximately 45,000 miles per hour before fragmenting over the region north of Cape Cod Bay.

When meteors enter Earth's atmosphere at high speeds, they typically burn up due to friction with air molecules. However, larger objects can survive long enough to create visible and audible events before breaking apart. The sonic boom occurs when a meteor travels faster than the speed of sound, generating pressure waves that produce the characteristic loud noise heard on the ground.

NASA's meteoroid environment office noted that most space rocks smaller than a football field will break apart in the atmosphere, though explosions in the air occur only on rare occasions. While meteor sightings are relatively common, events that produce sonic booms loud enough to be heard across such a wide area are less frequent.

The widespread nature of the reports suggested the meteor was traveling at significant speed when it entered the atmosphere. Residents across the affected region took to social media to share their experiences and discuss the unusual sounds. NASA's confirmation provided clarity for those who had heard the unexplained noise.

The potential presence of meteorite fragments in the vicinity of Cape Cod Bay could provide scientists with material for further study. According to NASA data, about 17,000 meteorites fall to Earth annually, though most remain undiscovered.

hero.headline: Blast kills dozens in rebel-held Myanmar village near Chinese border
hero.body:
A large explosion killed dozens of people in a rebel-held village in Myanmar near the Chinese border. Insurgents said the blast was caused by explosives being used for mining in the area.

The explosion occurred in a village controlled by rebel forces opposed to Myanmar's military government. The insurgents attributed the blast to mining operations using explosives close to the border with China.

Myanmar has been engulfed in conflict since the military seized power in 2021, sparking armed resistance across the country. Various ethnic armed groups and pro-democracy militias have controlled territory in border regions, particularly in areas near China.

The death toll from the explosion reached into the dozens, though exact casualty figures were not immediately available. The village's status as rebel-controlled territory has complicated access to the site and verification of the full scale of the disaster.

Mining operations in Myanmar's border regions have become a source of revenue for both military forces and insurgent groups during the ongoing civil conflict. The use of explosives in such operations poses significant risks to nearby civilian populations.

The blast comes as Myanmar's conflict continues with no resolution in sight. Multiple armed groups control different parts of the country, with fighting particularly intense in border areas where ethnic minorities have long-standing grievances against the central government.

China shares a lengthy border with Myanmar and has economic interests in the region, though it was not immediately clear whether Chinese authorities had responded to the explosion so close to their territory. The area near the Chinese border has seen significant instability as various armed factions vie for control of strategic and economically valuable territory.

cards.headline: Nearly 800 arrested after Champions League riots injure dozens of police in France
cards.teaser: Hundreds were arrested and dozens of police officers injured after clashes following a Champions League match.
cards.body:
Nearly 800 people were arrested following violent clashes with police after a Champions League match in France. The confrontations left 219 people injured, including 57 police officers.

The scale of the arrests and injuries made it one of the most serious incidents of sports-related violence in recent French history.

cards.headline: Colombia votes in presidential election that could reshape US relations
cards.teaser: Colombians began voting in a high-stakes presidential election testing the legacy of the country's first leftist leader.
cards.body:
Colombians are casting ballots in the first round of a presidential election that will determine the country's direction on peace and US relations. The vote comes after months of tension between outgoing leftist President Gustavo Petro and US President Donald Trump, with candidates offering starkly different visions for the nation's future.

The election serves as a referendum on Petro's policies a decade after Colombia signed a historic peace agreement with the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (Farc). Voters must choose between candidates with radically diverging approaches to addressing the country's decades-long conflict.

cards.headline: Cave survivors help search for two men still missing in Laos
cards.teaser: Five men have been rescued from a narrow, flooded cave in Laos, but efforts continue to locate two more.
cards.body:
Five men have been rescued from a flooded cave system in Laos, with two others still missing. The survivors are assisting rescue teams with their knowledge of the cave conditions and layout.

Divers continue navigating through narrow, water-filled tunnels filled with sharp rocks and collapse hazards to reach the remaining two men. The first rescue occurred on Friday, followed by the freeing of four more miners who had been trapped for 10 days.

cards.headline: South Africa confirms World Cup team will depart after visa confusion
cards.teaser: After uncertainty, the government confirmed the South African team will leave for Mexico following visa issues.
cards.body:
South Africa's government confirmed the national team will depart for Mexico after a day of uncertainty over visa issues. A minister said the country was made to look like fools over the World Cup visa problems.

The team's departure had been in doubt due to complications with travel documentation. The government resolved the issues, allowing the squad to travel as scheduled.

cards.headline: Trump suggests rally after artists drop out of US Freedom 250 festival
cards.teaser: President Trump called for cancellation of a White House-linked festival after most headliners withdrew.
cards.body:
President Trump has suggested canceling the US Freedom 250 festival after most of its headliners withdrew from the White House-linked event. He proposed holding a Make America Great Again rally as an alternative.

Several performers, including Young MC, Poison frontman Bret Michaels, and country singer Martina McBride, dropped out of the concert. The artists cited concerns that the event would be politically focused.

cards.headline: Pence calls Trump administration fund for political targets deeply offensive
cards.teaser: Former Vice President Mike Pence criticized a $1.8 billion settlement fund established by the Trump administration, calling it deeply offensive.
cards.body:
Former Vice President Mike Pence said he hopes the Trump administration will drop what he called a deeply offensive $1.8 billion fund. The Anti-Weaponization Fund has sparked alarm inside the White House, according to reports.

The settlement fund has attracted a list of would-be applicants seeking compensation. Pence's public criticism of the fund represents a rare rebuke from the former vice president of a Trump administration initiative.

cards.headline: Xavier Becerra leads California governor race ahead of primary
cards.teaser: Xavier Becerra holds a big lead in the California governor race just days before the primary election.
cards.body:
Xavier Becerra has pulled ahead in polling for California governor with days remaining before the primary. The race has raised questions about whether Democrats could be shut out of the general election under California's top-two primary system.

Candidates for both the governor's race and Los Angeles mayor made weekend campaign pushes ahead of the vote. The primary will determine which two candidates advance to the general election regardless of party affiliation.

cards.headline: Georgia town uses novel legal strategy to block ICE detention facility
cards.teaser: A Georgia town's approach to fighting a planned ICE jail has impressed legal experts reviewing the case.
cards.body:
The town of Social Circle in Georgia has filed a federal lawsuit against plans to convert a warehouse into a large immigration detention center. The lawsuit uses a "public nuisance" legal argument that goes beyond strategies employed in other recent cases, which have primarily relied on claims that environmental impact assessments were not properly conducted under federal law.

Legal experts say the town's approach could have significant implications for other communities facing similar detention facility proposals. The novel legal arguments in Social Circle's complaint have drawn attention from lawyers across the country considering how to challenge their own local detention center plans.

cards.headline: Israel Day Parade returns to New York with heightened security
cards.teaser: The annual Israel Day Parade took place in Manhattan with thousands gathering and a significant police presence.
cards.body:
Thousands of people gathered for the Israel Day Parade in Manhattan. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani did not attend the event but pledged a large police presence for security.

The parade resulted in street closures across Manhattan. The event returned this year against what organizers described as a changed backdrop, though specific circumstances were not detailed in available reports.

cards.headline: Police officer seriously injured after being struck by stolen police car
cards.teaser: A police officer suffered serious injuries and a man was arrested on suspicion of attempted murder after an incident involving a stolen police vehicle.
cards.body:
A PSNI officer was seriously injured after being struck by a stolen police car during an incident in which a shot was fired. A man has been arrested on suspicion of attempted murder in connection with the incident.

The officer remains in serious condition following the attack.

cards.headline: Chinese Lung Cancer Drug Reduced Death Risk by 34% in Late-Stage Trial
cards.teaser: A drug from Chinese pharmaceutical company Akeso showed significant survival benefits in a clinical trial presented at an international oncology conference.
cards.body:
Ivonescimab, developed by Akeso and Summit Therapeutics, demonstrated a 34 percent reduction in death risk for patients with squamous cell lung cancer when combined with chemotherapy. The drug outperformed existing PD-1 inhibitor treatments in the late-stage clinical trial conducted in China, with results presented at an oncology conference in Chicago.

The trial results underscore China's growing prominence in pharmaceutical development and biotechnology research, as the country increasingly contributes to global advances in cancer treatment innovation.

cards.headline: China's Biotechnology Growth Raises Concerns Over US Industry Leadership
cards.teaser: Clinical trials from China drew attention at an international oncology conference as the country's pharmaceutical sector expands rapidly.
cards.body:
Clinical trials conducted by Chinese pharmaceutical companies drew significant attention at an international oncology conference in Chicago. The presentations demonstrated China's expanding capacity to execute large-scale trials and develop new treatments, marking a notable shift in the global pharmaceutical landscape.

Chinese biotechnology firms are gaining market share in a sector traditionally dominated by American and European companies. Industry observers view this development as evidence that U.S. leadership in pharmaceutical research and drug development may be weakening.

cards.headline: Horror Film Backrooms Earns $82 Million as Young Audiences Return to Theaters
cards.teaser: The low-budget horror movie from a 20-year-old filmmaker drew strong attendance from younger moviegoers.
cards.body:
Backrooms earned $82 million in ticket sales, demonstrating that young audiences will attend theaters for certain films. The horror movie cost $10 million to produce and came from a filmmaker who is 20 years old.

The box office performance added to evidence that younger demographics have not abandoned theatrical releases entirely. Industry analysts view the results as an indication that theaters can still attract youth audiences when films match their interests.

cards.headline: Airbnb Expands Beyond Home Rentals to Include Hotels, Car Rentals, and Groceries
cards.teaser: The home-sharing platform added multiple new services as CEO Brian Chesky pursues a broader vision for the company.
cards.body:
Airbnb recently added car rentals, groceries, and hotels to its platform, expanding well beyond its original home-sharing model. Brian Chesky, the co-founder and chief executive, continues to explore ways to redesign the application.

The additions mark a significant shift for a company that built its business on peer-to-peer home rentals. The inclusion of hotels represents a particularly notable change, bringing Airbnb into direct competition with traditional booking platforms.

cards.headline: Joby Tests Electric Air Taxi in New York City Ahead of Regulatory Approval
cards.teaser: An aviation startup demonstrated an all-electric aircraft in Manhattan, though public flights remain years away.
cards.body:
Joby completed a test flight of its electric air taxi in New York City. The aviation startup and the Trump administration aim to replace helicopters with electric aircraft for urban transportation.

The vehicles must still pass extensive testing before the public can use them. Regulatory approval and safety certification remain significant hurdles for the emerging air taxi industry, despite successful demonstrations in major cities.

cards.headline: United Airlines Flight Returns After Bluetooth Device Name Triggers Security Alert
cards.teaser: A flight from Newark to Spain turned around mid-flight after the name of a passenger's Bluetooth speaker raised security concerns.
cards.body:
United Airlines flight UA236 from Newark to Palma de Mallorca turned back shortly after takeoff on Saturday night due to a security concern involving a Bluetooth device. The crew repeatedly asked passengers to disable their Bluetooth connectivity as the aircraft headed back to Newark.

The Boeing 767 was forced to abandon its transatlantic journey about an hour after departure because of the alert triggered by a Bluetooth speaker's broadcast name.

cards.headline: Apple pushes smart glasses launch to late 2027, delays Vision headset updates
cards.teaser: Apple has delayed its entry into the smart glasses market and postponed updates to its Vision product line.
cards.body:
Apple has pushed back the launch of its smart glasses product to late 2027, according to reports. The company is developing glasses designed to look like regular frames, representing its next wearable product following the Apple Watch.

The company has also delayed other vision products, with a Vision Air model now expected to arrive by 2029 and the Vision Pro 2 reportedly delayed to 2028. The delays come ahead of the company's developer conference. Apple's approach to smart glasses aims to disrupt the glasses market similarly to how it entered the watch market.

cards.headline: James Bond game becomes sales hit despite mixed critical reception
cards.teaser: The new James Bond video game has achieved strong sales performance across PlayStation 5 and Steam platforms.
cards.body:
007 First Light has become a significant sales hit and is already being discounted on PlayStation 5 and Steam. The game has attracted attention for representing a potential bright future for James Bond video games.

Developer IO Interactive, known for the Hitman series, created the game as a prequel following young Bond in his pre-00 days. The Guardian's review praised it as "a triumphant James Bond game made by obsessive fans," highlighting how IO Interactive's expertise with stealth gameplay, globe-trotting narratives, and distinctive visual style made them well-suited to the franchise.

cards.headline: MSI unveils gaming desktop with holographic AI companion display
cards.teaser: MSI has introduced what it calls the first gaming desktop featuring an agentic AI companion with holographic display.
cards.body:
MSI showed the MEG Vision X2 AI Plus, which the company describes as the world's first gaming desktop with an agentic AI companion. The system features a holographic Holostage display and includes what MSI calls AI Jinni, an AI hub designed specifically for MSI personal computers.

The desktop includes a holographic AI capsule attached to the system. MSI has positioned the product as integrating artificial intelligence capabilities directly into gaming hardware through the companion display technology.

cards.headline: Black founders secure highest quarterly funding since 2022
cards.teaser: Black entrepreneurs raised their largest amount of quarterly funding in four years, though barriers to capital access persist.
cards.body:
Black founders raised their highest amount of quarterly funding since 2022, according to Crunchbase data. The improvement marks a significant upturn in venture capital directed toward Black-led companies following years of reduced investment.

Despite this progress, substantial challenges persist. Gené Teare, Crunchbase's head of research, identified key barriers that continue to hinder Black founders, including limited access to investor networks, relationships, and early introductions—structural obstacles that remain even as funding levels recover.

cards.headline: James Webb telescope discovers stellar bar in early universe
cards.teaser: The James Webb Space Telescope has found a stellar bar structure in the early universe that challenges existing models.
cards.body:
The James Webb Space Telescope has identified a stellar bar in the early universe that breaks established rules about galaxy formation. The discovery was reported by researchers analyzing JWST observations.

Stellar bars are elongated structures of stars found in some galaxies. The presence of such a structure in the early universe presents questions about how quickly galaxies could develop these features after the Big Bang.

cards.headline: Enhanced Games featuring athletes on performance drugs presents new sports model
cards.teaser: A sporting competition where most athletes used performance enhancing drugs has concluded, backed by tech industry support.
cards.body:
The Enhanced Games took place in Las Vegas, featuring swimmers and other athletes where a majority of competitors were on performance enhancing drugs. The event involved steroids and other substances typically banned in traditional sports competitions.

The competition may represent a new business model that the tech industry is prepared to support. The event attracted financial backing as organizers promoted a different approach to athletic competition that openly permits substance use.

hero.headline: Spurs eliminate defending champion Thunder in Game 7, advance to NBA Finals
hero.teaser: Victor Wembanyama and the San Antonio Spurs defeated Oklahoma City 111-103 to win the Western Conference finals.
hero.body:
The San Antonio Spurs defeated the defending champion Oklahoma City Thunder 111-103 in Game 7 of the Western Conference finals, earning a spot in the NBA Finals against the New York Knicks. Game 1 is scheduled for Wednesday in San Antonio.

Victor Wembanyama led the Spurs with 22 points and seven rebounds in the decisive game. The 7-foot-4-inch French center was named series MVP and became emotional after the victory, reflecting on what the achievement meant to him personally.

"Realizing that some part of a childhood dream is going to come true," Wembanyama said when asked about his emotional reaction. "We're still hungry, we want more. This feeling is so powerful, I can't explain it."

However, the Spurs' victory was far from a one-man effort. Julian Champagnie contributed 20 points and made six three-pointers, while Dylan Harper provided crucial minutes off the bench. Luke Kornet, Wembanyama's backup, made a significant defensive play with a block at the rim during the fourth quarter when the Thunder mounted a comeback attempt.

"They don't know how much I love them, and everyone stepped up tonight," Wembanyama said of his teammates.

The Thunder, playing without injured guard Jalen Williams due to a hamstring injury, fought until the final moments. However, they were forced to take difficult three-pointers from well beyond the arc as time expired, and the Spurs sealed the win with a breakaway dunk.

Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, the reigning NBA MVP, had a strong performance for Oklahoma City with 35 points and nine assists. However, none of his teammates scored more than 20 points as the Thunder failed to defend their championship.

Thunder coach Mark Daigneault acknowledged the loss while looking ahead: "You have to grow from every experience, including the tough ones. And it's the NBA – there are tough ones. We can also be really disappointed. There's nobody that we don't think we can beat, respectfully."

The Spurs will face the Knicks in a Finals matchup with historical significance. The last time these teams met in the NBA Finals was in 1999, when San Antonio won the series 4-1.

Champagnie reflected on the team's accomplishment after the game, saying: "We never knew if we were going to get this far but when you've got the greatest player in the world things happen."

For much of the season, many questioned whether the defending champion Thunder had any weaknesses. The arrival and impact of Wembanyama ultimately made the difference in a thrilling seven-game series that propelled San Antonio to the championship round.

cards.headline: Ball State freshman football player dies at 18 after shooting
cards.teaser: Gavin Yates-Lyons, a freshman defensive back on the Ball State football team, died Saturday at the age of 18.
cards.body:
Gavin Yates-Lyons, an 18-year-old freshman defensive back for Ball State University's football team, died Saturday following a shooting incident.

Yates-Lyons was a member of the Cardinals' recruiting class and had been preparing for his first season of collegiate competition in the Mid-American Conference.

cards.headline: Iga Swiatek upset at French Open as all defending singles champions eliminated
cards.teaser: Marta Kostyuk defeated four-time champion Iga Swiatek to reach the French Open quarterfinals.
cards.body:
Iga Swiatek's dominance at Roland Garros came to an abrupt end on her 25th birthday, falling to 15th seed Marta Kostyuk 7-5, 6-1 in the fourth round. The No. 3 seed delivered one of her worst performances on Court Philippe-Chatrier, where she had won four titles in five years before this tournament.

Kostyuk's victory marks her first quarterfinal appearance at the French Open. With Swiatek's loss, all defending singles champions have been eliminated from this year's tournament, making her the latest high-profile casualty at Roland Garros.

cards.headline: Norway wins first ice hockey world championship medal with overtime upset of Canada
cards.teaser: Norway defeated Canada 3-2 in overtime to capture bronze at the ice hockey world championship.
cards.body:
Norway achieved a historic milestone by capturing its first-ever ice hockey world championship medal. The team defeated Canada 3-2 in overtime during the bronze medal game, stunning the favored Canadians in the extra period.

This victory represents a breakthrough moment for Norwegian ice hockey on the world stage, securing the nation's first podium finish at the prestigious international tournament.

cards.headline: Oklahoma City pledges to improve after Game 7 loss ends title defense
cards.teaser: The Thunder vowed to get better after losing to San Antonio in the Western Conference finals.
cards.body:
The San Antonio Spurs defeated the defending champion Oklahoma City Thunder 111-103 in Game 7 of the Western Conference Finals, advancing to the NBA Finals. Victor Wembanyama led the Spurs to victory, addressing a key weakness the Thunder lacked during their championship season.

The Spurs will now face the New York Knicks in the NBA Finals, with Game 1 scheduled for Wednesday in San Antonio.

cards.headline: Automated ball-strike system malfunctions during Athletics-Yankees game
cards.teaser: The ABS system incorrectly called a strike on a pitch that replay showed missed the zone.
cards.body:
The automated ball-strike system experienced a rare malfunction during a game between the Oakland Athletics and New York Yankees. A pitch to Athletics left fielder Tyler Soderstrom was confirmed as a strike even though replay showed it missed the zone by less than an inch.

The glitch represents an unusual failure for the ABS technology. The incorrect call went against Oakland in the game against the Yankees.

cards.headline: Tennessee softball coach accused of handshake line comment to opposing player
cards.teaser: Texas Tech player says Volunteers coach Karen Weekly made a comment about her transfer during postgame handshakes.
cards.body:
Texas Tech third baseman Taylor Pannell accused Tennessee coach Karen Weekly of telling her she made a mistake transferring from Tennessee during the postgame handshake line. The comment allegedly came after Tennessee's 2-1 extra-inning victory at the Women's College World Series.

Weekly called the accusation a lie. Pannell, who previously played for Tennessee, said the coach made the remark following the Volunteers' win over the Red Raiders.

hero.headline: Foster Sylvers, R&B Singer and Member of The Sylvers, Dies at 64
hero.body:
Foster Sylvers, a singer and member of the R&B group The Sylvers, has died at age 64. The musician had been battling metastatic prostate cancer.

Sylvers performed as part of The Sylvers, a family group that gained prominence in the R&B music scene. The group included several siblings who performed together during their career.

As a child musician, Sylvers became known for his work with the family ensemble. The Sylvers released multiple albums and charted songs during their active years, contributing to the R&B genre during their era.

Foster Sylvers also pursued solo work alongside his group activities. His performances as both a solo artist and group member spanned decades in the music industry.

The cause of death was attributed to complications from metastatic prostate cancer, a disease he had been fighting. Metastatic prostate cancer occurs when cancer cells spread from the prostate to other parts of the body.

The Sylvers were part of a wave of family groups that achieved success in R&B and soul music. The group's recordings and performances reached audiences throughout their career, establishing them within the genre's history.

Sylvers' death adds to recent losses in the music community. His work with The Sylvers remains part of the recorded history of American R&B music from the period when the group was active.

Family members and colleagues in the music industry have acknowledged his passing. Sylvers is survived by his siblings, several of whom were also members of The Sylvers during the group's performing years.

cards.headline: Matt Brown, Alaskan Bush People Star, Dies at 42
cards.teaser: The Discovery docudrama series star was found dead in a river, according to his brother.
cards.body:
Matt Brown, a cast member on Discovery's docuseries "Alaskan Bush People," has died at age 42. His brother Bear announced the death in a video posted on social media, saying that Matt's body was found in a nearby river.

Bear indicated that the death appeared to be suicide. Matt was a prominent figure on the show, which documented his family's life in Alaska.

cards.headline: Ronald LaPread, Co-Founding Member of the Commodores, Dies at 75
cards.teaser: The bassist, who lived in Auckland for four decades, was a founding member of the Motown group.
cards.body:
Ronald LaPread, a co-founding member and former bassist of the Commodores, has died at age 75. He died in Auckland, New Zealand, where he had resided for the past 40 years.

LaPread was a founding member of the Commodores, the Motown group known for hits during the 1970s and 1980s. As the group's bassist, he contributed to the ensemble's sound during their commercial peak. After his time with the band, he relocated to New Zealand, where he spent the remainder of his life.

cards.headline: Dua Lipa Marries Callum Turner in London Ceremony
cards.teaser: The singer wed actor Callum Turner during an intimate ceremony, wearing a bridal skirt suit.
cards.body:
Dua Lipa and Callum Turner have married in an intimate ceremony held in London. The legal wedding took place with the singer wearing a skirt suit described as old Hollywood-inspired.

The ceremony was a private affair attended by close associates. Lipa, a Grammy-winning pop artist, and Turner, an actor, have been in a relationship prior to the wedding. The couple chose London as the location for their legal marriage ceremony.

cards.headline: KSI Leaves Sidemen YouTube Collective After 13 Years
cards.teaser: The British YouTube star, whose real name is Olajide Olatunji, has departed the group he joined in 2013.
cards.body:
KSI has left the Sidemen, a YouTube collective he helped form and remained part of for 13 years. The creator, born Olajide Olatunji, had been with the group since its founding in 2013.

The Sidemen is a British YouTube group known for collaborative content and individual channels with millions of subscribers. KSI became one of the platform's most prominent figures during his tenure with the collective. His departure marks the end of his association with the group that helped establish his online presence.

cards.headline: Peter Gabriel Releases New Song 'A Hard Lesson' on Blue Moon
cards.teaser: The musician continues his i/o project with another single tied to the full moon.
cards.body:
Peter Gabriel has marked the blue moon with the release of a new song called 'A Hard Lesson.' The track is part of his ongoing i/o project, which ties musical releases to the lunar calendar.

Gabriel continues to issue new singles with each full moon as part of this structured release strategy. The latest addition to the series arrived with the blue moon event.

cards.headline: Protests Erupt Outside Delaney Hall ICE Facility
cards.teaser: Demonstrations followed reports of a hunger strike at the immigration detention center.
cards.body:
Large-scale protests have taken place outside Delaney Hall, an Immigration and Customs Enforcement facility. The demonstrations followed reports of a hunger strike by detainees over conditions described as inhumane.

The protests led to police response and crackdowns outside the facility. The demonstrations represent opposition to immigration enforcement policies and detention conditions. The facility has become a focal point in debates over immigration detention practices.

hero.headline: Pence criticizes Justice Department anti-weaponization fund
hero.teaser: Former Vice President Mike Pence called the Department of Justice's new fund a bad idea and urged the Trump administration to eliminate it.
hero.body:
Former Vice President Mike Pence criticized the Department of Justice's recently created anti-weaponization fund during a television interview. Pence told NBC News that he believes the fund is a bad idea from the start.

Pence encouraged the Trump administration to drop the fund entirely. He made the comments during an appearance on a Sunday news program, where he discussed current Justice Department policies.

cards.headline: Jill Biden says former president was slowing down before dropping reelection bid
cards.teaser: Former first lady Jill Biden said in her first post-White House interview that she observed her husband slowing down before he ended his 2024 presidential campaign.
cards.body:
Former first lady Jill Biden told CBS News that former President Biden was slowing down in the period before he dropped his 2024 presidential bid. She made the comments in her first interview since leaving the White House.

Jill Biden spoke with CBS News Sunday correspondent Rita Braver in an interview released Sunday. She said she never saw signs that her husband was experiencing cognitive or mental decline, according to the interview.

cards.headline: Trump calls for cancellation of America 250 concert after artist withdrawals
cards.teaser: President Trump urged organizers to cancel the planned 250th birthday concert and replace it with a political rally after multiple performers pulled out.
cards.body:
President Trump called for the concert celebrating America's 250th birthday to be cancelled after several scheduled performers withdrew from the event. Young MC, Poison frontman Bret Michaels and country singer Martina McBride cited concerns that the event would become political.

Trump's Interior Secretary Doug Burgum defended the concert series as nonpartisan, dismissing criticism from the artists who backed out. Burgum complained that some musicians "seem to have segmented their audiences" and declined to publicly identify donors who funded the event.

cards.headline: Senator Kim describes week of ICE facility protests as most difficult of his life
cards.teaser: Senator Andy Kim called the past week of clashes between law enforcement and protesters outside a New Jersey immigration detention center exceptionally difficult.
cards.body:
Senator Andy Kim described the past week of clashes between law enforcement officers and demonstrators protesting conditions inside a federal immigration detention center as one of the most difficult of his life. The New Jersey Democrat made the statement during a Sunday interview.

Kim met with protesters outside Delaney Hall in Newark last weekend. The demonstrators had gathered in solidarity with detained migrants at the federal facility, leading to confrontations with law enforcement over the course of the week.

cards.headline: Pence comments on GOP direction after Texas Senate race
cards.teaser: Former Vice President Pence said the Republican Party has lost its way while also criticizing Democrats during an interview about Texas politics.
cards.body:
Former Vice President Pence said during a Sunday interview that his party has lost its way, while also attacking Democrats by saying they have lost their minds. Pence made the comments while discussing the upcoming US Senate race in Texas.

During an appearance on Meet the Press, NBC News correspondent Kristen Welker pressed Pence on who he would support in the Texas Senate race. The race involves a Republican candidate described as facing scrutiny, following a win by Attorney General Ken Paxton.

cards.headline: Tech executives continue courting Trump administration
cards.teaser: Leaders from major technology companies have spent over a year working to win President Trump's favor through meetings and donations.
cards.body:
Tech leaders' lobbying efforts have yielded concrete results. President Trump reversed course on an AI executive order just hours before signing it, abandoning a planned requirement for government safety reviews of new artificial intelligence models. The president cited American competitiveness and competition with China as reasons for the decision.

The reversal occurred despite public concerns about AI risks and expert warnings that new models pose security threats. The decision effectively allows the technology industry to advance AI development without regulatory oversight, demonstrating the influence tech executives have gained through their sustained engagement with the Trump administration.

cards.headline: Analysis examines US deterrence policy shift on Taiwan
cards.teaser: A policy analysis argues that Washington's move toward transactional foreign policy has altered strategic calculations regarding Taiwan.
